chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in a lengthy report, that he said:
O Abu Hamza, indeed from us, after the Qa'im, there will be eleven Mahdis from the descendants of Husain (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَحَدَ عَشَرَ: Eleven, indicating the number of Mahdis following the Qa'im.
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the twelfth Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who will rise to establish justice.
key_terms.مَهْدِيًّا: Mahdi (guided one), referring to the Imams who are guided by God.
key_terms.وَلَدِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Descendants of Husain, referring to the progeny of Imam Husain ibn Ali (peace be upon him).

ai.seo_question: How many Mahdis will there be after Imam al-Qa'im according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes a specific eschatological sequence where eleven Mahdis from the progeny of Imam Husain (a.s.) follow the primary Imam al-Qa'im. While the exact identity of these eleven is subject to scholarly interpretation, the hadith underscores the enduring continuity of divine guidance and the unique spiritual authority of the Husaynid line within Shia tradition. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the post-occultation or post-appearance leadership structure in Twelver Shi'ism.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 504 - Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ja’far Himyari has narrated from his father from Muhammad bin Abdul Hamid and Muhammad bin Isa from Muhammad bin Fudail from Abu Hamza from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) a lengthy report, in which he said: “
O Abu Hamza, after Imam Qaim (a.s) there will be twelve Mahdis from us, the descendants of Imam Husain (a.s).”
